task_3.title: Support per-test skipped entries in the short summary
task_3.description: Pytest 8.3.0 adds a terminal option that lets users disable folding of skipped tests in the short summary. The default compact grouped summary remains unchanged, while the new mode shows each skipped test separately with its own identifier and any available skip reason.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can control whether skipped tests are folded together in the short test summary, so they can either keep the existing grouped output or view each skipped test as an individual summary entry.

expectation.grounded: Pytest should expose a `--no-fold-skipped` command-line option for terminal reporting. In the short summary, skipped outcomes should remain folded by default, but when `--no-fold-skipped` is provided, skipped reports should be listed individually using each skipped report's nodeid and skipped status formatting, with the skip reason included when present.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to switch skipped-test reporting in the short summary from grouped output to per-test output. By default the summary should stay compact, and opting out of folding should make every skipped test visible as its own line together with any available reason.

constraints.grounded: The new option must only affect how skipped results are rendered in the short summary. Default behavior must remain folded skipped summaries, and unfolded output must preserve normal short-summary status styling while emitting one line per skipped report. If a skipped report has no reason text, it should still be shown individually without a reason suffix.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing behavior unless the user explicitly disables skipped-summary folding, and limit the change to skipped-item presentation in the short summary. Other reporting categories and execution behavior should not change.

behavior: Add a `--no-fold-skipped` CLI option that disables folding of skipped tests in the short summary.
Preserve the current default behavior in which skipped tests are folded into grouped summary entries.
When skipped folding is disabled, print each skipped test on its own short-summary line using the test's node identifier instead of an aggregated count entry.
Append the skip reason to each individually reported skipped line when a reason is available.
acceptance_criteria: When skipped results are included in the short summary without `--no-fold-skipped`, skipped tests with the same location and reason should continue to appear as a single folded summary entry.
When skipped results are included in the short summary with `--no-fold-skipped`, each skipped test should appear on its own summary line with its node identifier.
When an individually reported skipped test has a recorded reason, the short summary line should include that reason.
When an individually reported skipped test has no recorded reason, the short summary should still show the skipped test as a standalone entry without failing.

task_2.title: Support Marker Keyword Argument Selection in -m Expressions
task_2.description: Pytest 8.3.0 extends marker-expression based test selection so users can filter tests by custom marker keyword arguments and values when using `-m`. The upgrade adds call-style marker matching semantics while keeping the feature limited to marker expressions and a constrained set of literal value types.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that marker-based test selection supports filtering by marker keyword arguments and values in addition to marker names, so users can target or exclude tests based on custom marker metadata supplied on the marker.

expectation.grounded: When evaluating `pytest -m` expressions, a marker identifier may optionally include keyword arguments, and the expression should match items whose markers of that name contain the requested keyword/value pairs. Supported literal values are integers, unescaped string literals, booleans, and `None`. A call-style marker match should return false when no marker of that name exists or when none of the matching markers contains all requested keyword/value pairs. Existing boolean composition with `and`, `or`, and `not` must continue to work around these marker calls.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to select tests with `-m` not only by marker name, but also by specific marker attributes such as IDs, flags, or other marker metadata. Marker filters should behave predictably in combined expressions, and only clearly supported literal value types should be accepted.

constraints.grounded: The call-style syntax applies to marker expressions used by `-m`, not keyword expressions used by `-k`. Marker call arguments are limited to keyword arguments; malformed names, reserved keywords, unsupported literal forms, or escaped string content should be rejected as invalid expressions. Matching must remain non-destructive: plain marker-name checks without keyword arguments must keep their prior behavior.
constraints.conceptual: This enhancement is scoped to marker selection only and must not broaden unrelated expression features. Invalid filter syntax should fail fast instead of being interpreted loosely, and existing name-only marker selection should continue to work unchanged.

behavior: A `-m` marker expression can now include a marker name followed by keyword filters in parentheses.
Within a marker call, all supplied keyword filters must be satisfied by the same marker instance for that call to match.
If an item has multiple markers with the same name, the marker call matches when any one of those markers satisfies all requested keyword/value pairs.
Marker-call matching supports integer values, including negative integers, unescaped string literals, boolean values, and `None`.
If a requested marker name is absent on an item, or present only with non-matching keyword values, that marker call evaluates to false.
Boolean operators in marker expressions continue to compose marker-name checks and marker-call checks in the usual way.
Call parameters are not supported for keyword-expression matching, so call-style syntax outside marker expressions remains invalid.
acceptance_criteria: When a test item is marked with a custom marker carrying keyword metadata, using `pytest -m` with that marker name and matching keyword filters should include that item.
When the marker name matches but one or more requested keyword values differ, the `-m` expression should not match that item.
When multiple keyword filters are supplied in one marker call, the call should match only if one marker instance of that name contains all of those keyword/value pairs together.
When an item has several markers with the same name, the `-m` expression should match if any one of those markers satisfies the requested keyword filters.
When marker-call filters use supported integers, strings, booleans, or `None`, the expression should be accepted and evaluated normally.
When marker-call filters use invalid argument names, unsupported literal forms, or escaped string syntax, the expression should be rejected as invalid.
When users continue to write name-only marker expressions, selection behavior should remain unchanged.
When users attempt call-style parameters in keyword-based selection rather than marker-based selection, the expression should be rejected instead of being treated as a supported filter.

task_1.title: Separate XFAIL traceback output from XFAIL summary reporting
task_1.description: The upgrade introduces an explicit opt-in flag for showing tracebacks for expected failures and restores the default behavior where XFAIL entries can appear in summaries without printing their tracebacks. XFAIL traceback formatting now follows the configured traceback style only when explicitly enabled.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that XFAIL traceback display is controlled independently from XFAIL summary reporting, so users can keep XFAIL entries in terminal summaries without automatically printing traceback details unless they explicitly opt in.

expectation.grounded: Pytest 8.3.0 must provide a `--xfail-tb` command-line option that enables traceback output for `xfailed` results in terminal reporting. When `--xfail-tb` is not set, XFAIL tracebacks must be suppressed even if XFAIL results are included in summary reporting via `-rx` or `-ra`. When `--xfail-tb` is set, XFAIL traceback rendering must follow the active `--tb` mode (`auto`, `long`, `short`, `line`, `native`, or `no`), and `--tb=no` must still suppress traceback output.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to see which tests were expected to fail without being forced to view full XFAIL tracebacks. XFAIL tracebacks should appear only when explicitly requested, and they should respect the configured traceback display style.

constraints.grounded: Existing traceback handling for ordinary test failures must remain governed by `--tb`. XFAIL summary visibility through existing reporting flags must continue to work, but those flags must no longer implicitly enable XFAIL traceback sections. No XFAIL traceback output should be emitted unless the user opts in with `--xfail-tb` and traceback output is not disabled.
constraints.conceptual: The change should narrow XFAIL output without reducing normal failure diagnostics or removing existing XFAIL summary information. Opt-in traceback behavior for expected failures must remain consistent with the user's overall traceback display preferences.

behavior: Adds a `--xfail-tb` CLI flag to opt into traceback output for expected failures.
Stops showing XFAIL traceback sections by default when expected failures are reported in terminal summaries.
Decouples XFAIL traceback output from `-rx` and `-ra`, so those flags only affect summary reporting for XFAIL results.
Applies the selected `--tb` traceback style to XFAIL tracebacks when `--xfail-tb` is enabled.
Keeps XFAIL tracebacks suppressed when `--tb=no`, even if `--xfail-tb` is enabled.
acceptance_criteria: When a test run contains expected failures and the user enables `-rx` or `-ra` without `--xfail-tb`, it should include XFAIL results in the summary output without printing XFAIL traceback details.
When a test run contains expected failures and the user passes `--xfail-tb`, it should print XFAIL traceback output in the terminal.
When `--xfail-tb` is enabled together with a specific `--tb` mode such as `line`, XFAIL traceback output should use that selected traceback style.
When `--xfail-tb` is enabled together with `--tb=no`, it should not print XFAIL traceback output.
When ordinary test failures occur, their traceback display should continue to follow `--tb` regardless of whether `--xfail-tb` is set.

task_4.title: Adopt generic third-party plugin terminology in pytest plugin reporting
task_4.description: The upgrade updates pytest's user-facing plugin reporting so console output describes distribution-discovered plugins as third-party plugins instead of referring to setuptools, while preserving the existing plugin listing behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest's user-facing version and help output refers to distribution-discovered plugins using generic third-party plugin terminology instead of setuptools-specific wording.

expectation.grounded: When pytest emits plugin distribution details from `Config.pluginmanager.list_plugin_distinfo()` through its help/version reporting, it should label that section as third-party plugin registration information rather than setuptools registration information. The existing per-plugin distribution details remain visible for each discovered plugin.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should use modern, generic language when showing installed external plugins, so users see them described as third-party plugins without any outdated setuptools-specific wording.

constraints.grounded: Only the user-visible terminology for the distribution-backed plugin section should change. The section should still appear only when plugin distribution info exists, and each discovered plugin should continue to be reported with the same observable metadata it exposed before.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should rename the plugin category in output without changing which plugins are shown, when they are shown, or the practical meaning of the reported plugin details.

behavior: Verbose pytest output that includes installed plugin distribution information now describes that section as third-party plugins instead of setuptools-registered plugins.
Each discovered plugin continues to be listed with its package identity and source location in the same reporting flow.
If no distribution-discovered plugins are available, pytest should continue omitting that plugin-reporting section.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest reports installed plugin distribution information, it should identify the section using third-party plugin terminology rather than setuptools-specific terminology.
When one or more external plugins are discoverable from package metadata, pytest should continue listing each plugin's distribution information and location.
When no plugin distribution information is available, pytest should not add an empty or renamed plugin section to the output.

task_6.title: Show full function arguments in -vvv failure output
task_6.description: The upgrade changes pytest failure rendering so very high verbosity no longer ellipsizes function argument values in traceback output. It also separates argument truncation from local-variable truncation, preserving existing abbreviated output at lower verbosity while allowing full argument representations when users request highly verbose diagnostics.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest failure output shown at very high verbosity no longer truncates displayed function arguments in tracebacks, while keeping lower-verbosity failure output safely abbreviated.

expectation.grounded: When failure rendering includes function arguments, `ExceptionInfo.getrepr` and `FormattedExcinfo` should support a `truncate_args` control that is independent from `truncate_locals`. In standard failure output, verbosity greater than 2 (`-vvv` and above) should disable argument truncation so `ReprFuncArgs` shows full argument representations, while lower verbosity should continue to use safe truncated representations.
expectation.conceptual: At very high verbosity, traceback argument displays should show complete values instead of ellipsized ones. Normal verbosity should keep shortening long argument values so failure output remains manageable.

constraints.grounded: This change applies to displayed function arguments only and must not implicitly change local-variable truncation behavior. Argument truncation should remain enabled by default unless high-verbosity failure formatting or an explicit API caller disables it. Existing traceback style, filtering, and exception-chain behavior should remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Only the visibility of function argument values at high verbosity should change. Other traceback formatting behavior and the default condensed output should continue to behave as before.

behavior: `ExceptionInfo.getrepr` forwards an argument-truncation setting separately from local truncation settings.
`FormattedExcinfo` can render function arguments either in truncated form or in full, depending on the argument-truncation setting.
Standard pytest failure rendering disables function-argument truncation when verbosity is greater than 2, making `-vvv` and higher show full argument representations.
At lower verbosity levels, long function argument values continue to appear in safely abbreviated form.
Local-variable truncation remains controlled independently and is not removed just because function arguments are shown in full.
acceptance_criteria: When a failing test includes a very long function argument value and pytest is run with `-vvv` or higher, the traceback's function-argument display should show the full argument representation rather than an ellipsized version.
When the same failure is shown at default verbosity or with verbosity at 2 or below, the function-argument display should still abbreviate overly long values.
When failure rendering is configured to show locals, changing function-argument truncation should not by itself disable or alter local-value truncation behavior.
When code uses the exception-rendering API with function-argument display enabled, argument truncation should be independently configurable from local-variable truncation.

task_5.title: Improve virtual environment detection during collection
task_5.description: Pytest 8.3.0 changes virtual environment detection to rely on the standard pyvenv.cfg marker instead of platform-specific activation script layouts, so default collection more reliably recognizes and excludes virtual environment directories across platforms such as mingw Python on Windows.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest reliably recognizes Python virtual environment roots across platform-specific and nonstandard layouts so it does not mistakenly treat virtual environment directories as normal project content during default test discovery.

expectation.grounded: Pytest's virtual environment detection should treat a directory as a virtual environment root when that directory contains `pyvenv.cfg`. Directories without `pyvenv.cfg` should not be identified as virtual environments based on activation-script locations or names, and OS-level errors while checking the marker file should result in a safe non-detected outcome rather than an exception.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should identify virtual environments using the standard metadata file that Python environments provide, regardless of whether their folder layout looks Windows-style or Unix-style, and it should avoid surfacing filesystem-detection failures as user-facing errors.

constraints.grounded: The detection contract should be based on the presence of `pyvenv.cfg` and should not require scanning `bin` or `Scripts` for activation scripts. The change should preserve failure safety by treating unreadable or erroring paths as not positively detected virtual environments.
constraints.conceptual: Virtual environment recognition should be layout-agnostic, should not depend on activation script conventions, and should fail conservatively instead of disrupting collection.

behavior: A directory containing `pyvenv.cfg` is recognized as a Python virtual environment root.
A directory without `pyvenv.cfg` is not recognized as a virtual environment solely because it contains `bin`, `Scripts`, or activation-script files.

Virtual environment detection no longer depends on platform-specific activation directory structure, improving recognition for environments such as mingw Python on Windows that use Unix-style layouts.
If checking for the virtual environment marker triggers an `OSError`, pytest treats the directory as not detected as a virtual environment instead of raising from detection.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest evaluates a directory that contains `pyvenv.cfg`, it should recognize that directory as a virtual environment root during collection-related detection.
When pytest evaluates a virtual environment on Windows that uses a Unix-style layout but includes `pyvenv.cfg`, it should still recognize it as a virtual environment.
When pytest evaluates a directory that lacks `pyvenv.cfg`, it should not classify that directory as a virtual environment based only on activation-script files or `bin`/`Scripts` folders.

When filesystem access to the virtual environment marker check fails with an OS-level error, pytest should continue without surfacing a detection exception and should treat the directory as not positively identified as a virtual environment.

task_7.title: Improve bound-method assertion introspection readability
task_7.description: The 8.3.0 update makes failed assertion output easier to read when bound instance methods are involved by showing a concise method-oriented representation instead of a verbose bound-method object representation, while leaving unrelated value rendering behavior unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that failed assertions involving bound instance methods present concise, readable introspection output instead of verbose bound-method object representations.

expectation.grounded: When pytest formats rewritten assertion failures that involve a bound method call, the explanation should render the bound method using its method name rather than the full bound-method representation. This behavior applies to bound methods and should be visible in AssertionError output generated from assertion introspection.
expectation.conceptual: When an assertion fails around a call to an instance method, the failure explanation should show a compact, human-readable method reference so users can understand the failing expression quickly.

constraints.grounded: Only the representation of bound methods in assertion introspection should change. Existing safe representation behavior for other values, including normal objects, classes, and non-bound callables, should remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Improve readability for bound methods without broadly changing how unrelated values are displayed in assertion failure output.

behavior: Failed rewritten assertions should display bound methods by method name instead of a verbose bound-method object representation.
Assertion explanations for expressions such as instance method calls should remain traceable to the original call chain while removing redundant bound-method formatting.
Values that are not bound methods should continue to use the existing safe representation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a rewritten assertion involving an instance method call fails, the failure explanation should show the method reference compactly by name rather than as a verbose bound-method object.
When the failing expression includes a method obtained from an instance, the introspection output should still make the call relationship understandable after the formatting change.
When assertion introspection formats regular objects, classes, or non-bound callables, it should preserve prior display behavior.

task_8.title: Add timezone-aware JUnit XML suite timestamps
task_8.description: The JUnit XML report should emit a timezone-aware testsuite timestamp so external systems do not misinterpret suite start times as UTC or another unintended timezone.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JUnit XML reports include timezone information in the testsuite timestamp so downstream CI and reporting systems can interpret the reported suite start time correctly.

expectation.grounded: When pytest generates a JUnit XML report, the testsuite `timestamp` attribute should be an ISO 8601 datetime that includes timezone information. The timestamp should still represent the suite start time, but it must be timezone-aware rather than a naive datetime string.
expectation.conceptual: JUnit XML output should expose the suite start time with an explicit timezone offset, allowing consumers to read the timestamp unambiguously across different environments.

constraints.grounded: Continue exposing the testsuite `timestamp` as a valid ISO 8601 value in the XML report, preserve its meaning as the suite start time, and avoid changing unrelated report fields or overall JUnit XML structure.
constraints.conceptual: Only improve the timestamp's clarity and interoperability; the report should remain compatible with existing JUnit XML consumers aside from now providing the missing timezone context.

behavior: Pytest JUnit XML reports now emit a timezone-aware value for the testsuite `timestamp` attribute instead of a timezone-naive datetime.
The reported timestamp includes an explicit UTC offset corresponding to the environment's local timezone at the recorded suite start time.
Consumers of the JUnit XML report can distinguish local-time timestamps from UTC because the serialized timestamp now carries timezone information.
acceptance_criteria: When a JUnit XML report is generated, the testsuite `timestamp` attribute should include timezone information as part of its ISO 8601 datetime value.
When the test suite runs on a machine configured for a non-UTC timezone, the generated testsuite timestamp should include that timezone offset rather than appearing as a naive local datetime.
When downstream tools parse the JUnit XML report, they should be able to determine the intended timezone of the suite start timestamp without applying external assumptions.

task_9.title: Restore reporting of higher-scoped fixture teardown failures on early stop
task_9.description: Pytest 8.3.0 restores reporting for teardown failures from higher-scoped fixtures when a run stops early because `--maxfail` or `--stepwise` halts execution after a test failure. The upgrade ensures active fixture finalizers still run during shutdown and their failures are surfaced as errors instead of being dropped.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that teardown failures from higher-scoped fixtures are still executed and reported when pytest stops a run early because `--maxfail` is reached or `--stepwise` halts progression after a failing test.

expectation.grounded: When pytest is running with `--maxfail` or `--stepwise` and a failure causes the session to stop, teardown for active higher-scoped fixtures must still be performed before shutdown. If a fixture finalizer fails during that teardown, pytest must report it as an error in addition to the original failing test outcome, rather than aborting in a way that loses the teardown failure from pytest's reported results.
expectation.conceptual: Early-stop modes should not hide fixture cleanup failures. If a test failure causes the run to stop, pytest should still finish relevant fixture teardown work and surface any teardown failure as an error alongside the original failure.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the stop behavior of `--maxfail` and `--stepwise`: pytest should still stop scheduling later tests once the stop condition is met. The change is limited to teardown and reporting for already-active higher-scoped fixtures, and must not turn skipped or unexecuted later tests into executed tests.
constraints.conceptual: Keep early termination semantics unchanged while making shutdown reporting complete. The fix should add missing teardown error visibility without resuming normal execution of the remaining test suite.

behavior: If a test failure causes pytest to stop because `--maxfail` has been reached, pytest still tears down active higher-scoped fixtures before ending the run.
If teardown of an active higher-scoped fixture fails during that shutdown, pytest reports an additional error instead of losing the teardown failure.
The same teardown-error reporting behavior applies when pytest stops early because of `--stepwise`.
Later tests that would have run after the stop condition remain unexecuted; the change affects teardown completion and reporting, not test scheduling.
acceptance_criteria: When a test using a higher-scoped fixture fails and `--maxfail` stops the session, pytest should still execute teardown for that active fixture before exiting.

When that teardown fails after `--maxfail` or `--stepwise` has stopped the run, pytest should include the teardown failure in its reported outcomes as an error in addition to the original test failure.
When the stop condition is reached, pytest should not continue running subsequent tests solely because teardown reporting has been fixed.
When no teardown failure occurs, early-stop behavior under `--maxfail` and `--stepwise` should remain unchanged.

task_10.title: Support sequence-like inputs in pytest.approx
task_10.description: Upgrading to 8.3.0 fixes pytest.approx so custom ordered sequence-like objects are handled consistently during approximate comparisons and mismatch reporting, instead of breaking during failed comparison detail generation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `pytest.approx()` supports ordered custom sequence-like values in the same way it supports built-in sequences, including when a comparison fails and pytest needs to show mismatch details.

expectation.grounded: When `pytest.approx(expected, rel=None, abs=None, nan_ok=False)` receives an expected value that is sequence-like because it provides indexed access and a size, and it is not `str` or `bytes`, it should be treated as a supported ordered sequence input through the same approximate-comparison path used for sequence containers. Element-wise comparison detail generation should recurse through that input without raising unrelated representation or length errors.
expectation.conceptual: Approximate equality should work for custom ordered sequence containers, and a failing comparison should still produce a normal, user-readable mismatch result instead of failing while formatting the assertion output.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing handling for `Decimal`, mappings, NumPy arrays, and unsupported non-ordered collections. Inputs such as `str` and `bytes` must not be treated as numeric sequences for `pytest.approx()`, and unordered collection inputs should continue to be rejected.
constraints.conceptual: Limit the change to ordered sequence-like inputs and keep all other supported and unsupported input categories behaving as they did before.

behavior: `pytest.approx()` should recognize ordered sequence-like objects beyond `list` and `tuple` when they expose indexed access and length and are not string or bytes values.
Approximate comparisons against those sequence-like objects should continue to behave element by element under the configured tolerances.
Internal recursive processing used to build comparison details should traverse those sequence-like objects successfully instead of assuming only built-in sequence container types.
If a comparison against a supported sequence-like object fails, pytest should report the approximate mismatch normally rather than surfacing a secondary error from assertion-detail rendering.
acceptance_criteria: When a custom ordered sequence-like object is passed to `pytest.approx()`, it should be accepted as a supported approximate-comparison input.
When two supported sequence-like values differ only within the configured tolerance, the comparison should evaluate as equal.
When two supported sequence-like values differ beyond the configured tolerance, the comparison should evaluate as unequal and the failed assertion output should remain readable and intact.
When `pytest.approx()` is given an unsupported unordered collection, it should continue to reject that input rather than treating it as an ordered sequence.

task_12.title: Skip abstract test classes during collection
task_12.description: Pytest 8.3.0 fixes collection behavior so abstract test classes are no longer treated as runnable tests. This prevents collection-time failures caused by trying to instantiate abstract base classes while preserving execution of concrete subclasses.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that abstract test classes are not collected as runnable tests, including abstract unittest.TestCase subclasses, so collection only considers concrete implementations and does not fail when abstract base classes are present.

expectation.grounded: During class-based discovery, pytest should treat abstract classes as non-test classes even if they otherwise match test class naming or nose-style collection rules. During unittest integration, pytest_pycollect_makeitem should ignore abstract unittest.TestCase subclasses instead of collecting them into UnitTestCase nodes. Concrete subclasses that are no longer abstract should remain collectable under the existing public discovery rules.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to create abstract base classes for shared test behavior without pytest attempting to run those base classes. Only concrete subclasses should be collected and executed, and abstract classes should be skipped cleanly during discovery.

constraints.grounded: The change should only affect classes that are abstract at collection time. Existing collection behavior for concrete test classes, including normal pytest classes and concrete unittest.TestCase subclasses, should remain unchanged. Abstract classes should be skipped rather than causing instantiation-related collection errors.
constraints.conceptual: Do not broaden or narrow test discovery beyond excluding abstract classes. Projects that already rely on concrete test classes being collected should continue to behave the same, aside from removal of failures caused by abstract bases being considered runnable tests.

behavior: A class that otherwise looks like a pytest test class is not collected if it is abstract.
An abstract unittest.TestCase subclass is not collected as a unittest test case.
Pytest no longer attempts to instantiate abstract test base classes during collection.
Concrete subclasses derived from abstract test bases are still eligible for collection and execution once they implement all abstract requirements.
Collection succeeds without raising abstract-class instantiation errors when abstract test bases are present in the test hierarchy.
acceptance_criteria: When a project defines an abstract class whose name matches pytest's class discovery rules, pytest should skip that class during collection instead of treating it as a runnable test class.
When a project defines an abstract unittest.TestCase subclass, pytest should not collect or instantiate that abstract class during unittest discovery.
When a concrete subclass implements all abstract methods from an abstract test base, pytest should collect and run the concrete subclass normally.
When abstract and concrete test classes coexist in the same inheritance chain, collection should complete successfully without abstract-class instantiation failures.
When no abstract classes are involved, class-based and unittest-based collection behavior should remain consistent with prior concrete-class behavior.

task_11.title: Stabilize reused setup failure tracebacks
task_11.description: Pytest 8.3.0 fixes a regression where repeated failures caused by the same higher-scope fixture or collector setup error could accumulate increasingly long tracebacks across affected items. The update preserves the original traceback when cached setup failures are re-raised and introduces an internal plugin-visible change to cached failure metadata so it carries both the exception and traceback.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that repeated test failures caused by a shared higher-scope fixture setup error or collector setup error report a stable traceback for every affected item, while preserving compatibility expectations for plugins that inspect cached setup failures.

expectation.grounded: When `FixtureDef` reuses a cached setup failure, it should re-raise the original exception with its original traceback instead of re-raising the exception in a way that extends the traceback chain. When `SetupState` reuses a stored collector setup failure for later items, it should also re-raise the original exception with its original traceback. Fixture cache hits should be recognized for equal cache keys, with fallback to identity comparison if equality raises `ValueError` or `RuntimeError`. Plugins that inspect `FixtureDef.cached_result[2]` or failure entries in `SetupState.stack` must expect a tuple containing the exception and traceback rather than only the exception.
expectation.conceptual: Repeated failures caused by one shared setup problem should look the same for each affected test item instead of growing noisier over time. Reused setup failures should preserve their original failure context, and plugin integrations should continue to understand the failure metadata exposed by the upgraded version.

constraints.grounded: Do not change which fixture or collector setup failures surface to users, and do not alter the exception type raised for those failures. Successful fixture caching behavior must remain intact. For cache-key objects whose equality check raises `ValueError` or `RuntimeError`, cache matching must safely fall back to object identity.
constraints.conceptual: The change should stabilize how reused setup failures are reported without changing which tests fail, what kind of failure they report, or how successful setup and caching behave. Edge cases around unusual cache-key objects should remain safe and non-disruptive.

behavior: A cached higher-scope fixture setup failure is stored together with its traceback and re-raised with that original traceback for each affected test item.
A remembered collector setup failure is stored together with its traceback and re-raised with that original traceback for later items that share the same failed setup path.
Repeated items affected by the same cached setup failure no longer accumulate longer traceback output from prior re-raises.
Fixture cache reuse is determined by cache-key equality when that comparison succeeds, with fallback to identity comparison if equality raises `ValueError` or `RuntimeError`.
Plugin-visible cached failure metadata for `FixtureDef.cached_result[2]` and `SetupState.stack` failure entries now includes both the exception object and its traceback.
acceptance_criteria: When multiple test items depend on the same higher-scope fixture that fails during setup, each affected item should fail with the same exception and a stable-length traceback.
When multiple collected items share a collector whose setup fails, each affected item should report that setup failure without the traceback growing from one item to the next.
When a cached setup failure is re-raised, it should preserve the original traceback context instead of appending a fresh traceback chain on each reuse.
When fixture cache keys compare equal, the cached result should be reused; if equality comparison raises `ValueError` or `RuntimeError`, cache matching should fall back to identity comparison.
When plugins inspect cached setup failure entries exposed by the upgraded version, they should be able to retrieve both the exception and its traceback.

task_13.title: Restore package-scoped fixture reuse ordering
task_13.description: Pytest 8.3.0 fixes a regression introduced in pytest 8 where parametrized package-scoped fixtures were no longer ordered to maximize reuse across modules in the same package. After upgrading, pytest should again group collected items by active package-scope parameter so fixture setup and teardown happen once per parameter value across the package whenever reuse is possible.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that parametrized package-scoped fixtures are reused across all applicable test modules in the same package before pytest tears them down and switches to the next parameter value.

expectation.grounded: When pytest orders collected items that depend on a fixture declared with `scope="package"` and multiple parameter values, it should treat all items from modules in the same package as part of the same package-scoped grouping. Items sharing the same `FixtureArgKey` for that package-scoped parameter should be executed together so the fixture instance is set up once, reused across matching modules in the package, and torn down only after that parameter's grouped items complete.
expectation.conceptual: If several test modules in one package use the same parametrized package-scoped fixture, pytest should run every test for one parameter value across that package before moving to the next value, restoring efficient fixture reuse and avoiding unnecessary teardown and recreation between modules.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve scope boundaries: package-scoped grouping applies only within the same package, and existing ordering behavior for other scopes must continue to honor their own scope semantics. Non-parametrized cases and already-correct session, module, and class scope behavior must not regress.
constraints.conceptual: Improve ordering efficiency without changing fixture isolation rules or causing unrelated packages or scopes to share lifecycle state they should not share.

behavior: Parametrized fixtures declared with `scope="package"` participate in high-scope item reordering using the package as the grouping boundary rather than each individual module.
Tests from different modules inside the same package that require the same package-scoped fixture parameter are grouped into the same execution slice.

For a package-scoped fixture with multiple parameter values, pytest performs one setup and one teardown per parameter value for the package-level group when reuse is possible, instead of repeating setup and teardown module by module.
Items that do not have a relevant parametrized fixture key at the current scope continue to be reordered at lower scopes without breaking the package-level grouping behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given a parametrized `package`-scoped fixture used by tests in multiple modules within one package, when pytest orders and runs those tests, it should execute all items for one parameter value across the package before tearing that fixture instance down and starting the next parameter value.

When the suite is inspected with `--setup-plan`, package-scoped fixture lifecycle output should show reuse across modules in the same package for each parameter value rather than separate setup and teardown cycles for each module.
Tests in different packages should not be merged into the same package-scoped fixture lifecycle group.
Existing fixture ordering behavior for non-package scopes should remain consistent with their declared scope boundaries.

task_14.title: Restore rerun support for unittest.TestCase tests
task_14.description: Pytest 8.3.0 fixes a regression introduced in 8.2.2 where rerun-capable plugins could crash when re-running failing tests implemented with unittest.TestCase. The upgrade should preserve normal rerun behavior, avoid internal assertion failures, and surface the test's real outcome instead of a framework crash.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that failing tests defined on unittest.TestCase can be re-run by rerun-capable pytest plugins without crashing in pytest internals, and that reruns continue from the test's actual failure state rather than stopping on an internal assertion.

expectation.grounded: When pytest executes a TestCaseFunction for a unittest.TestCase-based test item and a plugin triggers a rerun, pytest should recreate or expose a valid unittest.TestCase instance for the rerun lifecycle. Re-running the item must not terminate with an internal AssertionError caused by an invalid missing testcase instance, and the observed failure or success should correspond to the test method itself.
expectation.conceptual: Rerunning a unittest-style test should behave like a normal second execution of that test. Users should see the test rerun according to plugin behavior, without pytest crashing internally or replacing the test's real result with a framework error.

constraints.grounded: The fix should preserve existing pytest unittest integration semantics outside the regression path, keep teardown safe for completed unittest-based items, and avoid changing the user-visible contract for non-rerun execution. It should not introduce a new public API requirement for rerun plugins.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be narrowly scoped to restoring correct rerun behavior for unittest-based tests, without altering how ordinary test runs behave or requiring users to change plugin usage.

behavior: Pytest should allow a unittest.TestCase-based test item to be executed again after teardown when a rerun plugin requests another run.
A rerun of a unittest-style test should start with a usable testcase object instead of failing due to invalid internal instance state.
When the test itself fails, pytest should report the test's own failure on that run rather than an internal assertion from the unittest bridge.
Rerun-capable plugins should be able to complete their configured rerun flow for unittest.TestCase items that failed on an earlier attempt.
acceptance_criteria: When a failing unittest.TestCase test is run with a pytest plugin that reruns failures, pytest should perform the rerun instead of aborting after the first attempt with an internal AssertionError.
When the rerun starts for a unittest-style test item, the test method should execute against a valid testcase instance.
When a unittest.TestCase test fails during execution, the reported failure should reflect the test's own failing behavior rather than an internal pytest unittest assertion.
When a unittest.TestCase test fails once and then succeeds on a rerun, pytest should allow that rerun path to complete normally.

task_16.title: Handle invalid pytest.raises match patterns cleanly
task_16.description: The upgrade improves error handling for invalid regular expressions passed to the `match` argument of `pytest.raises`. Instead of surfacing an internal regex compilation error during exception matching, pytest now fails cleanly with a user-facing usage failure that explains the `match` pattern is invalid while preserving normal behavior for valid patterns.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `pytest.raises(..., match=...)` handles invalid regular expression patterns as a user-facing pytest failure instead of exposing an internal regex error or traceback.

expectation.grounded: When `pytest.raises` is called with the `match` keyword, pytest should validate the supplied regex pattern before using it for exception matching. If the pattern is invalid, `pytest.raises` should stop with a clean pytest failure indicating that the `match` regex is invalid, rather than letting a raw `re.error` escape. For valid string patterns and compiled regex patterns, existing exception-matching behavior should continue unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Users should get a clear and direct failure when they provide an invalid regex to the `match` option of `pytest.raises`. The failure should point to misuse of the `match` argument, and valid matching behavior should continue to work as before.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the success semantics of `pytest.raises` for valid `match` values or for exception type matching itself. Invalid regex handling must be limited to the `match` argument and must avoid exposing an internal regex engine exception as the primary user-facing result.
constraints.conceptual: This change should only improve how invalid `match` patterns are reported. It should not alter normal exception assertion behavior for correctly formed patterns.

behavior: Calling `pytest.raises` with an invalid regex in `match` now produces a pytest-level failure instead of an uncaught `re.error`.
Regex validity is checked before the pattern is used to match the captured exception text.
The reported failure is user-facing and explicitly tied to an invalid `match` pattern.
Valid `match` patterns continue to participate in exception message matching with no intended behavioral change.
acceptance_criteria: When `pytest.raises` is given an invalid regex string through `match`, it should fail cleanly with a pytest failure that identifies the `match` pattern as invalid.
When an invalid `match` regex is provided, it should not surface a raw `re.error` traceback as the main user-facing outcome.
When `pytest.raises` is given a valid `match` pattern, it should keep matching raised exception text as before.
When `pytest.raises` is used without `match`, its exception-type assertion behavior should remain unchanged.

task_15.title: Stabilize custom pytest_report_teststatus verbose markup
task_15.description: Pytest 8.3.0 fixes terminal reporting for plugins that customize pytest_report_teststatus. Custom verbose status values can now carry explicit markup safely, including for failed and error outcomes, and invalid verbose return shapes are rejected explicitly instead of causing an internal crash during reporting.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that custom `pytest_report_teststatus` hooks can return a verbose status with explicit markup for reported outcomes, including `failed` and `error`, without crashing terminal output or summary rendering.

expectation.grounded: When `pytest_report_teststatus(report, config)` supplies its verbose value, pytest should accept either a plain string or a two-item `(word, markup)` value. The terminal reporter should render the provided word using the supplied markup when present, including in paths that display failed, error, xfailed, and xpassed results. If a plugin returns any other verbose shape, pytest should reject it explicitly instead of failing later with an internal rendering error.
expectation.conceptual: Plugins that customize test status text should be able to provide styled status labels, and those labels should appear consistently anywhere pytest prints that status. Invalid custom status data should produce a clear plugin-facing failure rather than an internal crash.

constraints.grounded: Existing hook implementations that return a string verbose value must remain supported, with pytest applying the default terminal styling for that status path. Only a string or a two-item verbose value containing a text label and a markup mapping is valid input for the verbose field.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must preserve current behavior for standard custom status labels while extending support for styled labels. It should tighten validation of malformed custom status output without regressing normal reporting.

behavior: Pytest now treats the verbose portion of `pytest_report_teststatus` as either plain text or a styled `(word, markup)` value.
When a styled verbose value is returned for categories such as `failed` or `error`, terminal reporting and summary generation render that styled word instead of crashing.
Styled verbose values are also honored in xfailed and xpassed reporting rather than being reduced to plain text with only default warning styling.
Malformed verbose return values from `pytest_report_teststatus` are rejected explicitly as invalid hook output.
acceptance_criteria: When a plugin returns a plain string as the verbose value from `pytest_report_teststatus`, pytest should continue to display that status using the normal default styling for that reporting path.
When a plugin returns a `(word, markup)` verbose value from `pytest_report_teststatus`, pytest should display the provided word with the provided styling in terminal output and summaries.
When a plugin returns category `failed` or `error` together with a styled verbose value, pytest should complete reporting without an internal terminal crash.
When a plugin returns a styled verbose value for xfailed or xpassed results, pytest should preserve that explicit styling in the rendered status label.
When a plugin returns an invalid verbose value shape from `pytest_report_teststatus`, pytest should fail explicitly because the hook output is invalid rather than crashing during later rendering.

task_17.title: Prevent Windows cache crashes during concurrent cache directory creation
task_17.description: The update hardens pytest's cache handling on Windows so concurrent creation of the cache directory no longer aborts execution. A benign rename collision that can surface as a Windows file-exists condition is now treated as an expected race, while unrelated filesystem failures still propagate.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that using pytest's cache functionality on Windows does not crash when the cache directory is created concurrently by another process or thread.

expectation.grounded: When the pytest Cache class encounters a concurrent cache-directory creation race on Windows during its directory replacement step, it should treat both the existing non-empty-directory collision and the Windows file-exists collision as recoverable race outcomes and continue without raising an exception. Other filesystem errors from the same operation should still be raised.
expectation.conceptual: Cache-related operations should remain stable under normal concurrent use on Windows. If another actor creates the cache directory first, pytest should continue normally instead of failing, while genuine filesystem problems should still be reported.

constraints.grounded: Only the specific concurrent directory-creation collision represented by the existing non-empty-directory condition or the Windows file-exists condition should be suppressed. The change must not broaden error suppression to unrelated OSError cases, and non-racing cache behavior must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to the harmless race condition. It must not hide real cache filesystem failures or alter normal cache behavior outside that concurrency edge case.

behavior: On Windows, a cache-directory rename collision that surfaces as a file-exists condition during concurrent creation is handled as a benign race instead of causing a crash.
The previously tolerated non-empty-directory collision remains treated as a benign concurrent-creation outcome.
Filesystem errors other than those concurrency-related collision conditions continue to propagate to the caller.
Runs that use pytest's cache functionality continue past the race condition without aborting when another actor creates the cache directory concurrently.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest uses its cache functionality on Windows and another process or thread creates the target cache directory concurrently, it should continue without raising a cache-creation exception.
When the concurrent cache-directory race on Windows appears as a file-exists collision during the directory replacement step, it should be treated as recoverable behavior.
When the same cache operation fails for a different filesystem reason, pytest should still raise the corresponding error.
When no concurrent cache-directory race occurs, cache behavior should remain unchanged from prior releases.

task_18.title: Fix parametrized fixture cache reuse for equal values
task_18.description: Pytest 8.3.0 restores expected reuse of parametrized fixture instances by comparing parameter values with equality before falling back to identity for comparison-unsafe objects. This prevents unnecessary fixture re-creation for distinct objects that represent the same parameter value while preserving compatibility for parameter types whose equality checks can raise.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that parametrized fixtures are cached and reused based on parameter value equality rather than only object identity, while still handling parameter types whose equality comparison is unsafe.

expectation.grounded: For parametrized fixtures created through pytest parametrization mechanisms such as `metafunc.parametrize(..., indirect=True)` and consumed through `@pytest.fixture`, cached fixture results should be treated as a cache hit when the current request's cache key compares equal to the stored cache key using `==`. If evaluating `==` raises `ValueError` or `RuntimeError`, pytest should fall back to identity comparison with `is`. When a cached fixture outcome is an exception, requesting the same cache key should re-raise the cached exception with its traceback instead of re-executing fixture setup.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should reuse a previously created parametrized fixture whenever a later parameter represents the same value, even if it is a different object instance. For parameter objects that cannot be compared safely with normal equality, pytest should degrade gracefully to identity-based matching. Repeated requests that hit a cached fixture failure should surface the same failure again without rerunning setup.

constraints.grounded: Do not require identical object instances for fixture cache reuse when parameter values compare equal. Do not fail cache lookup solely because parameter equality raises `ValueError` or `RuntimeError`; use identity matching in those cases. Preserve existing cached-result behavior for both successful fixture values and cached fixture exceptions.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must broaden cache reuse for equivalent parameter values without breaking parameter types that have non-standard equality behavior, and it must not change the fact that both successful and failed fixture outcomes remain reusable from cache.

behavior: Fixture cache lookup for parametrized fixtures now prefers `==` comparison between the requested cache key and the stored cache key.
If cache-key equality evaluation raises `ValueError` or `RuntimeError`, fixture cache lookup falls back to `is` identity comparison.
Distinct parameter objects that compare equal can now share the same cached fixture instance instead of causing redundant fixture setup.
Cached fixture exceptions are re-raised from cache with their stored traceback when the same cache key is requested again.
acceptance_criteria: When a scoped fixture is indirectly parametrized with separate objects that compare equal, repeated uses of that parameter value should reuse the cached fixture result instead of creating an additional fixture instance.

When parametrized fixture cache-key comparison with `==` raises `ValueError` or `RuntimeError`, pytest should continue normally by using identity-based cache matching rather than failing during cache lookup.
When a parametrized fixture request matches a cached successful result, pytest should return the cached value without rerunning fixture setup.
When a parametrized fixture request matches a cached failure, pytest should re-raise the cached exception with traceback rather than rerunning fixture setup.

task_19.title: Fix progress indicator alignment for parallel test runs
task_19.description: Pytest 8.3.0 fixes terminal progress reporting so progress indicators remain aligned during parallel execution with pytest-xdist, including when output events from multiple workers are interleaved. The update also ensures the final completed progress indicator is only shown after the full run has finished.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that terminal progress output stays aligned and readable during parallel execution, and that completed progress is not shown before the test run has actually finished.

expectation.grounded: When pytest runs with low-verbosity progress output enabled, including under pytest-xdist using `-n`, progress reporting should track unique completed test items by `nodeid`, handle interleaved worker events without corrupting the displayed progress, move the progress suffix onto a new line when it would exceed terminal width, and defer the final completed indicator such as percentage or full-count completion until the runtest loop has completed.
expectation.conceptual: Parallel execution should not cause the progress meter to drift, wrap unpredictably, or reach a completed state too early. Users should see stable incremental progress throughout the run and a single final completion display only when execution is fully done.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing progress display modes for both percentage-style and count-style output, avoid counting the same collected item more than once in progress totals, and do not change pass, fail, skip, or xfail result semantics while correcting terminal progress layout.
constraints.conceptual: The change should improve progress display accuracy only. It must not alter which test outcomes are reported or otherwise change the meaning of the test run beyond making progress reporting correct and readable.

behavior: Low-verbosity progress output updates based on uniquely reported test items, so interleaved events from parallel workers do not distort progress totals.
If the current line plus the progress suffix would exceed terminal width, pytest emits the progress indicator on a new line instead of letting the output overflow and misalign the display.
The overflow-handling behavior applies to both percentage-based progress and count-based progress displays.
The final completed progress indicator is emitted only after the overall test loop finishes, preventing premature `100%` or full-count completion while teardown work is still in progress.
acceptance_criteria: When running a large suite with `pytest-xdist -n` and progress output enabled, the progress indicator at the right edge of the terminal should remain visually aligned instead of wrapping inconsistently because of worker event ordering.
When multiple workers report results in an interleaved sequence, progress should advance according to unique completed test items and should not be overstated by duplicate reporting of the same item.
When progress is displayed as counts instead of percentages, it should follow the same alignment and overflow behavior as percentage mode.
When the test session completes, the final completion indicator should appear once and only after the run, including teardown completion, has finished.

task_20.title: Document pytest run detection via PYTEST_VERSION
task_20.description: Pytest 8.3.0 documents `PYTEST_VERSION` as the supported public signal for determining whether code is executing inside a pytest run. The upgrade clarifies how user code and integrations should detect pytest execution without relying on undocumented behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that code needing to know whether it is running under pytest can use a documented, supported signal to detect that condition.

expectation.grounded: Pytest 8.3.0 should publicly support `PYTEST_VERSION` as the environment variable to check when user code or integrations need to detect that execution is occurring within a pytest run. This upgrade should present `PYTEST_VERSION` as the documented detection contract instead of requiring private pytest APIs or ad hoc heuristics.
expectation.conceptual: Users should have one clear, supported way to tell whether execution is happening inside a pytest session: check the documented pytest version environment variable.

constraints.grounded: The upgrade should not require consumers to depend on internal pytest objects, stack inspection, or undocumented environment markers to detect a pytest run. The documented behavior should remain a detection contract centered on `PYTEST_VERSION`, with no implied change to unrelated runtime behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Detection should be simple and stable, and it should not force users to rely on implementation details or fragile guesses.

behavior: When code runs within a pytest invocation, `PYTEST_VERSION` is the documented environment signal available for detecting that pytest is active.
Code that needs pytest-run awareness may use the presence or value of `PYTEST_VERSION` as the supported public contract.
The upgrade clarifies detection semantics through documentation rather than introducing a separate new runtime API.
acceptance_criteria: When a developer needs to detect whether code is running under pytest, the supported guidance should direct them to `PYTEST_VERSION`.
When code executes during a pytest run, checking `PYTEST_VERSION` should be a valid documented way to detect that context.
When users adopt this upgrade, they should not need private pytest internals or undocumented markers to determine whether pytest is running.

task_21.title: Generalize plugin discovery terminology in user-facing documentation
task_21.description: The 8.3.0 update revises user-facing documentation to stop framing external pytest plugins as a setuptools-specific concept. Documentation should instead describe plugins using generic installed or third-party package terminology and align the explanation with modern Python distribution metadata discovery, without changing plugin loading behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that user-facing guidance for external pytest plugins no longer implies setuptools is required for plugin discovery or installation metadata, and instead describes such plugins in generic installed, external, or third-party package terms while preserving existing plugin behavior.

expectation.grounded: Pytest documentation and other user-facing references should describe external plugins as installed, external, or third-party plugins or packages rather than as setuptools entry points. The documented discovery model should align with distribution package metadata and modern metadata access mechanisms such as importlib.metadata, without changing pytest's plugin discovery, autoload, or assertion rewriting behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users should understand that pytest can discover plugins from installed packages through standard Python packaging metadata, and the documentation should not suggest that setuptools is the defining or required mechanism.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce runtime behavior changes to plugin loading, plugin autoload control, installable plugin support, or assertion rewriting for installed plugins. Keep public behavior unchanged and limit the update to terminology and explanatory guidance.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should clarify wording only. Existing plugin installation and discovery behavior must continue to work the same way for users.

behavior: User-facing references to externally installed pytest plugins are renamed from setuptools-specific wording to generic installed, external, or third-party plugin terminology.
The documented explanation of plugin discovery reflects distribution package metadata as the relevant concept rather than setuptools as a required tool.
Observable runtime behavior for plugin discovery, plugin autoloading, and assertion rewriting remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When users read pytest guidance about plugins, it should describe discoverable plugins as installed, external, or third-party packages rather than as setuptools entry points.
When users consult documentation about how pytest finds plugins, it should communicate that discovery is based on standard package metadata and should not imply setuptools is mandatory.
When users upgrade from 8.2.2 to 8.3.0, plugin loading behavior and related runtime outcomes should remain the same.

task_22.title: Expose CI-related environment variables in pytest help
task_22.description: Pytest 8.3.0 makes the command-line help surface the existing CI-related environment variables `CI` and `BUILD_NUMBER`, clarifying that they signal CI execution and affect whether summary information is truncated. This improves discoverability of environment-controlled behavior directly from `pytest -h`.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `pytest -h` documents the CI-related environment variables that affect pytest's output behavior, so users can discover from the CLI help that `CI` and `BUILD_NUMBER` indicate CI execution and influence summary truncation.

expectation.grounded: The `pytest -h` environment variable section should include `CI` and `BUILD_NUMBER`. The `CI` entry should describe that when the variable is present, regardless of its value, pytest recognizes the session as running in CI and does not truncate summary information. The `BUILD_NUMBER` entry should be documented as having the same effect as `CI`.
expectation.conceptual: Users reading pytest's command-line help should be able to see which environment variables mark the run as occurring in CI, and understand that either variable enables the same CI-oriented summary visibility behavior.

constraints.grounded: The change should be limited to exposing these public environment variable semantics in the CLI help. Existing help content for other environment variables should remain available, and the documented behavior must preserve that `CI` is triggered by presence rather than a specific value while `BUILD_NUMBER` remains equivalent to it.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve discoverability of existing CI-related behavior without changing unrelated help output or altering the meaning of other environment variables.

behavior: `pytest -h` now lists `CI` under environment variables.
The `CI` help entry indicates that merely setting the variable causes pytest to treat the run as occurring in CI and to avoid truncating summary information.
`pytest -h` now lists `BUILD_NUMBER` as an environment variable with behavior equivalent to `CI`.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `pytest -h`, the environment variable help should include an entry for `CI`.
When a user reads the `CI` entry in `pytest -h`, it should communicate that the variable's presence, regardless of value, enables CI mode and keeps summary information from being truncated.
When a user runs `pytest -h`, the environment variable help should include an entry for `BUILD_NUMBER` identifying it as equivalent to `CI`.

task_24.title: Adopt PyPy 3.9 to avoid flaky assertion-rewrite failures
task_24.description: This upgrade moves PyPy-based execution from 3.8 to 3.9 because PyPy 3.8 can intermittently fail during assertion rewriting and test module import due to a runtime garbage-collector bug. The change is about runtime compatibility and stability, not a new public API.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that PyPy-based use of the library runs on PyPy 3.9 instead of PyPy 3.8 so users do not encounter intermittent collection and import failures caused by the PyPy 3.8 runtime bug.

expectation.grounded: When pytest is executed on PyPy, the effective runtime baseline should be PyPy 3.9 rather than PyPy 3.8. Under that upgraded runtime, assertion rewriting and test module import should no longer be exposed to the known PyPy 3.8 garbage-collector issue that can surface as intermittent TypeError failures while compiling rewritten ASTs during collection. No new public pytest API, option, or configuration surface is introduced by this change.
expectation.conceptual: PyPy users should run the library on a current supported PyPy runtime so execution is stable and does not fail randomly because of a runtime defect. The upgrade should improve reliability without changing how users invoke or configure the library.

constraints.grounded: Do not require new user-facing commands, markers, or settings as part of the upgrade. Preserve existing public behavior on unaffected runtimes; the intended scope is replacing the problematic PyPy 3.8 runtime path with PyPy 3.9 and avoiding failures attributable to the older runtime.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the change limited to runtime compatibility and stability. Existing workflows should continue to behave the same aside from removing the flaky PyPy 3.8 failure mode.

behavior: PyPy-based execution is expected to target PyPy 3.9 instead of PyPy 3.8.
Intermittent failures during collection or module import that originate from PyPy 3.8 interacting badly with assertion rewriting should no longer occur under the upgraded runtime.
The upgrade does not add any new end-user API, flag, or configuration requirement.
acceptance_criteria: When the library is run in a PyPy environment, it should use PyPy 3.9 rather than PyPy 3.8.

When test modules are collected or imported under the upgraded PyPy environment, execution should not fail intermittently with a TypeError caused by rewritten AST compilation in the older PyPy runtime.
When users run the library on unaffected supported runtimes, they should not need to change their existing invocation or configuration.

task_25.title: Render changelog drafts directly during Sphinx doc builds
task_25.description: The documentation build now renders the changelog draft through the Sphinx towncrier extension instead of generating and including a temporary draft file. This makes changelog previews available in any Sphinx build environment, including hosted documentation builds, and removes the old temporary-file workflow.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Sphinx documentation builds always render the changelog draft preview automatically, without depending on a separately generated temporary draft file, so contributors and hosted doc builders see the same changelog preview behavior.

expectation.grounded: Documentation builds should obtain changelog draft content through `sphinxcontrib.towncrier.ext` during the Sphinx build, using the project's Towncrier configuration from `pyproject.toml`, with draft-version rendering enabled and empty sections included. The build should no longer depend on the deleted wrapper script or on the generated `_changelog_towncrier_draft.rst` file being present.
expectation.conceptual: When the docs are built, the pending changelog preview should appear automatically as part of the Sphinx output in all supported build environments. The preview should be generated from the project's release-note fragments directly during the build, even when there are no entries for some sections.

constraints.grounded: Do not require a pre-build command that writes a changelog draft file to disk. Do not rely on missing-include warning suppression for the old generated draft file. Preserve observable changelog draft output across local and hosted Sphinx builds, including release-tag documentation builds.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must remove reliance on temporary generated artifacts and keep the changelog preview consistently available wherever the documentation is built. It should avoid introducing environment-specific behavior or manual setup just to make the draft preview appear.

behavior: Sphinx documentation builds now render changelog draft content through the Towncrier Sphinx extension instead of a generated include file.
The previous helper workflow that created a temporary changelog draft file is removed, so the build no longer depends on that file existing.
Changelog draft rendering is configured to run in draft mode and to include empty sections in the generated preview.
The Towncrier draft generation uses the project root as its working directory and reads configuration from `pyproject.toml` during the docs build.
Because the draft is rendered directly by Sphinx, the changelog preview is available in environments beyond the old `tox` docs flow, including hosted documentation builds.
acceptance_criteria: When a contributor builds the Sphinx documentation locally, the changelog draft preview should be rendered without running a separate script to generate an intermediate file.
When the documentation is built in a hosted Sphinx environment such as a Read the Docs build, the changelog draft preview should still appear.
When no changelog entries exist for some configured sections, the draft preview should still render those sections as empty rather than omitting the preview entirely.
When the docs are built after this upgrade, successful changelog draft rendering should not depend on the presence of a pre-created `_changelog_towncrier_draft.rst` file.

task_26.title: Expose descriptions for all tox environments
task_26.description: The upgrade makes the project's tox environments self-describing when listed, so contributors can understand the purpose of every default and additional environment through `tox -av` without changing runtime library behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that every tox environment exposed by the project is described when contributors list environments, so no supported environment appears undocumented or unclear in purpose.

expectation.grounded: After upgrading to 8.3.0, invoking `tox -av` should show a human-readable description for each listed tox environment, including both default environments and additional environments, as well as factor-based variants such as interpreter-specific and feature-specific environments. The listing should communicate each environment's intended purpose through tox's environment descriptions.
expectation.conceptual: Environment discovery should be complete and understandable: when contributors ask tox to list available environments, every environment should clearly state what it is for.

constraints.grounded: This change should affect only the descriptive metadata surfaced by tox environment listings. Existing environment names, availability, invocation patterns, and the underlying actions performed by those environments should remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Improve discoverability without changing what the environments do or how developers use them.

behavior: Listing tox environments with `tox -av` now provides descriptions for environments that were previously undocumented.
Both standard test environments and auxiliary environments are expected to appear with purpose-oriented descriptions.
Descriptions should reflect factor-dependent variants so specialized environments remain distinguishable in the listing.
acceptance_criteria: When a contributor runs `tox -av`, it should display a description alongside every listed tox environment.
When default environments are listed, none of them should appear without an explanation of their purpose.
When additional or specialized environments are listed, each one should also include a clear purpose description.
When comparing behavior before and after the upgrade, the change should improve environment discoverability without altering the commands or roles associated with existing environments.

task_23.title: Adopt pytest 8.3.0 typing update and corrected package-scoped fixture ordering
task_23.description: Upgrade to pytest 8.3.0, which primarily modernizes annotations to Python 3.10+ syntax and also corrects how parametrized package-scoped fixtures are grouped during item reordering so fixture reuse matches package boundaries instead of individual test files.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to pytest 8.3.0 preserves compatibility with the library's Python 3.10+ annotation model and correctly groups parametrized package-scoped fixtures across tests in the same package so unnecessary setup and teardown churn does not occur between modules.

expectation.grounded: The upgraded behavior should align with pytest 8.3.0, where fixture-related public and semi-public annotations use Python 3.10+ forms, and parametrized fixture item reordering treats `Scope.Package` keys by package directory rather than by individual module path. When `reorder_items` processes parametrized fixtures, tests that share the same package-scoped fixture parameter within one package should remain grouped for execution, while existing session, module, class, and function scope semantics continue to apply.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, the dependency should behave like pytest 8.3.0: typing metadata follows modern Python annotation conventions, and tests that share the same package-level parametrized fixture should execute in a package-consistent grouping that avoids needless fixture recreation across files in the same package.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable meaning of fixture scopes other than the package-scope grouping fix. Session-, module-, class-, and function-scoped fixture behavior must remain consistent with prior pytest semantics, and non-parametrized items must not gain new ordering requirements solely from this update.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be narrowly compatible: it should improve package-scoped parametrized fixture scheduling without introducing unrelated execution-order changes or altering how other fixture scopes behave.
