behavior: Parametrized package-scoped fixtures are grouped using the package directory as their scheduling boundary instead of the individual test module file path.

Tests in different modules within the same package that share the same package-scoped fixture parameter can now be executed as a single grouped block, allowing reuse of the same package-scoped fixture instance.
The item reordering logic continues to minimize high-scope fixture setup and teardown churn, with ordering state updated consistently as grouped items are pulled forward.

The 8.3.0 source and exposed typing metadata use Python 3.10+ annotation forms such as builtin generics and union operators, without implying a new runtime API contract beyond the fixture-ordering correction.
acceptance_criteria: When tests in multiple modules under the same package use the same parametrized package-scoped fixture value, they should run in a grouping that reuses that package-scoped fixture instance instead of recreating it separately per module.
When parametrized fixtures use session, module, class, or function scope, the upgrade should preserve their existing scope boundaries and not reinterpret them as package-scoped behavior.
When a test item has no relevant parametrized fixture key at the current reordering scope, it should still remain eligible for lower-scope ordering without being dropped or duplicated.
When consumers inspect annotations or type-check against pytest 8.3.0 interfaces, they should encounter Python 3.10+ style annotations rather than legacy `typing.List` and `typing.Optional` forms.

task_28.title: Draft automated plugin bump pull requests until review
task_28.description: The upgrade changes the maintainer workflow for automatically generated plugin list update pull requests. Instead of requiring maintainers to close and reopen those pull requests to trigger CI, the automation should create them as draft pull requests and direct maintainers to mark them ready for review when they want CI to run.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that automatically generated plugin list update pull requests use a review-ready workflow that lets maintainers trigger CI by marking the pull request as ready for review, without needing to close and reopen it.

expectation.grounded: Automated plugin list update pull requests should be created as draft pull requests. The automation should leave maintainers an observable prompt on the pull request indicating that they should use GitHub's Ready for review action to trigger CI, replacing the previous close-and-reopen workaround.
expectation.conceptual: Automatically created dependency or plugin update pull requests should follow a GitHub-native draft-to-review flow so maintainers can intentionally start CI from the pull request UI when they are ready to review the change.

constraints.grounded: The workflow change applies to the GitHub automation that opens plugin list update pull requests. It must remove the need for maintainers to close and reopen those pull requests in order to trigger CI, and it should rely on the pull request draft status and Ready for review transition as the observable control point.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve the maintainer experience without changing library runtime behavior. The CI trigger path for automated update pull requests should be simpler and aligned with normal GitHub pull request interactions.

behavior: When the automation opens a plugin list update pull request, the pull request is created in draft state.
The automated pull request includes visible guidance telling maintainers to mark it ready for review to start CI.
Maintainers no longer need to close and reopen an automated plugin update pull request to trigger CI.
The transition from draft to ready for review becomes the intended action for activating CI on these automated pull requests.
acceptance_criteria: When an automated plugin list update pull request is created, it should appear as a draft pull request rather than an immediately reviewable pull request.
When maintainers view the automated pull request, they should see clear instruction that marking it Ready for review is the action that triggers CI.
When a maintainer marks the automated draft pull request as Ready for review, the workflow should use that transition as the CI trigger point.
When maintainers handle automated plugin update pull requests after the upgrade, they should not need to close and reopen the pull request to get CI to run.

task_27.title: Replace the deprecated trivial changelog category with audience-specific note types
task_27.description: Pytest 8.3.0 updates changelog note classification by removing the broad `trivial` category and replacing it with clearer audience-specific categories: `packaging`, `contrib`, and `misc`. This is a release-documentation and contributor-workflow change rather than a runtime behavior change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that release note classification no longer relies on the deprecated `trivial` category and instead uses the new audience-specific categories for packaging-related updates, contributor/process updates, and miscellaneous documented changes.

expectation.grounded: For pytest 8.3.0, changelog handling should treat `packaging`, `contrib`, and `misc` as the supported note categories replacing `trivial`. `packaging` should cover downstream redistribution and packaging-related updates, `contrib` should cover project contributor, development, and process news, and `misc` should cover documented updates that do not fit other sections. The provided code diff shows no production-code changes, so no runtime API, exception, warning, or execution behavior change is evidenced for this upgrade item.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, release notes should classify minor non-feature updates using clearer, audience-specific categories instead of a single vague bucket. Readers should be able to distinguish packaging updates, contributor/process updates, and miscellaneous notes, with no expected change to normal runtime behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not continue treating `trivial` as an active category for new changelog entries. Keep this change limited to release-note categorization and wording; based on the provided code diff, existing runtime behavior and public execution semantics should remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should only change how release notes are organized and described. It must not alter observable library behavior for normal users.

behavior: The previous `trivial` changelog category is removed as the catch-all category for minor documented updates.
A `packaging` category is available for notes intended for downstream packagers and redistributors.
A `contrib` category is available for notes about contributor-facing development and process changes.
A `misc` category is available for documented updates that do not fit other categories.
Changelog section naming and descriptions are clearer and more explicit for their intended audience.
acceptance_criteria: When a documented update concerns packaging or redistribution, it should be categorized under `packaging` rather than `trivial`.
When a documented update concerns contributor workflow, development practices, or project processes, it should be categorized under `contrib` rather than `trivial`.
When a documented update does not fit another section but should still be recorded, it should be categorized under `misc`.
When preparing or reading changelog entries after the upgrade, `trivial` should no longer be treated as a valid current category.
When upgrading from 8.2.2 to 8.3.0 for this change item, normal runtime behavior should remain unchanged.

task_29.title: Adopt the new Sphinx PR role and updated documentation extensions
task_29.description: The documentation toolchain was updated to use third-party Sphinx extensions instead of custom GitHub link roles. Pull request references now use `:pr:` rather than `:pull:`, GitHub issue and PR links are resolved through `sphinx_issues`, Towncrier draft changelog content is integrated directly into the docs build, and tagged Read the Docs builds can expose release-only content.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the documentation system and contributor-facing authoring conventions are updated for pytest 8.3.0 so GitHub pull request references use the new `:pr:` role, GitHub issue/PR links continue to resolve correctly, draft changelog content remains available in documentation builds, and release documentation builds preserve release-specific content handling.

expectation.grounded: The Sphinx documentation configuration should load `sphinx_issues` for GitHub-related roles and treat `:pr:` as the supported role for pull request references, replacing `:pull:`. Documentation builds should resolve GitHub references against the `pytest-dev/pytest` repository through the configured `issues_github_path`. The docs build should also expose Towncrier draft content through `sphinxcontrib.towncrier.ext`, using the project root and `pyproject.toml` configuration, and release-tagged Read the Docs builds should set the release tag context so release-only content is included. Documentation version metadata should continue to derive from `pytest.__version__`, with local-version suffixes excluded from the published docs version string.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, documentation authors should use the newer, shorter pull request role and expect GitHub references to render correctly without project-specific custom link role wiring. The documentation build should continue to surface draft changelog information and distinguish tagged release builds from non-release builds, while leaving pytest's runtime behavior unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Do not preserve `:pull:` as the primary pull request role for documentation authoring. Keep GitHub issue and pull request references mapped to the pytest repository, keep draft changelog generation available in docs builds even when draft sections are empty, and avoid introducing any change to pytest's execution APIs or runtime behavior because the update is limited to documentation configuration.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should remain backward-safe for pytest users at runtime, with all impact confined to documentation authoring and rendering. Documentation references and release-build content must stay consistent and not lose existing issue, pull request, or changelog visibility.

behavior: Documentation authored with `:pr:` should resolve to GitHub pull request links for the pytest repository.
GitHub-related documentation roles should be provided by `sphinx_issues` rather than by manually configured extlinks.
Documentation builds should resolve issue and pull request references against `pytest-dev/pytest`.
Towncrier draft changelog entries should be available as part of the docs build using the repository's Towncrier configuration from `pyproject.toml`.
Draft changelog rendering should remain available even when there are no draft entries for a section.
Tagged Read the Docs builds should be identifiable as release builds so release-only documentation content can be included.
Published docs version metadata should omit local build suffixes while still deriving from the installed pytest version.
acceptance_criteria: When a documentation page uses the `:pr:` role for a pytest pull request number, the rendered docs should link to the corresponding GitHub pull request.
When documentation pages use supported GitHub issue or pull request roles, the generated links should target the `pytest-dev/pytest` repository.
When draft changelog content is included in the docs, the build should obtain that content from the project's Towncrier configuration without requiring custom in-repo role handling.
When a Read the Docs build is triggered for a tagged release, release-specific documentation content should be included as a release build.
When pytest 8.3.0 is adopted, users running pytest should observe no runtime or public API behavior change attributable to this documentation update.

task_30.title: Exclude expected-failure tests from coverage reporting
task_30.description: The 8.3.0 update changes the library's coverage-reporting behavior so tests intentionally marked as expected to fail no longer affect reported coverage totals. This reduces noise and flakiness in coverage results without introducing a supported runtime feature change in the provided artifacts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading from 8.2.2 to 8.3.0 preserves existing runtime behavior while adopting the updated coverage-reporting semantics in which tests marked as expected to fail no longer influence the reported coverage level.

expectation.grounded: The upgrade should reflect the 8.3.0 coverage configuration change: tests marked as expected to fail are excluded from coverage measurement so partially executed, missing, or flaky execution in those tests does not lower reported coverage. No public pytest API, CLI, exception, or assertion-behavior change is evidenced by the provided diff artifacts.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, coverage reports should be more stable because known expected-failure tests no longer count against coverage, and application-facing test execution behavior should otherwise remain the same.

constraints.grounded: Do not infer or require new runtime features, changed failure semantics, new warnings, or new command-line behavior from this upgrade. The available evidence only supports a coverage-accounting change related to expected-failure tests, and the provided code diff does not show additional behavioral changes.
constraints.conceptual: Treat this upgrade as a reporting-only change, not as a functional change to how users run tests or how application code behaves under the library.

behavior: Coverage totals should exclude tests intentionally marked as expected to fail.
Partially executed or non-executed expected-failure tests should no longer depress the reported coverage percentage.
No user-visible runtime or public API behavior change is evidenced by the provided release note and diff inputs beyond the coverage-reporting adjustment.
acceptance_criteria: When coverage is produced after upgrading to 8.3.0, tests marked as expected to fail should not contribute executed or missing lines to the reported coverage result.
When expected-failure tests are flaky or only partially run, the reported coverage level should remain unaffected by those tests.
When using the upgraded library for normal test execution, users should not observe a new runtime feature or changed external behavior attributable to the provided upgrade evidence.

task_31.title: Remove legacy BPO documentation role support
task_31.description: Pytest 8.3.0 removes the legacy Sphinx extlinks-based Python bug tracker role from its documentation setup and standardizes issue references on GitHub-backed roles. This is a documentation authoring and docs-build compatibility change rather than a runtime behavior change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that documentation used with pytest 8.3.0 no longer relies on the deprecated `:bpo:` role and instead uses supported GitHub issue cross-references so documentation remains compatible with the updated docs toolchain.

expectation.grounded: The pytest 8.3.0 documentation configuration no longer enables `sphinx.ext.extlinks`, so the `:bpo:` reStructuredText role is no longer provided. Documentation should use the GitHub-oriented roles exposed by `sphinx_issues`, including `:issue:` for issue references and `:pr:` for pull request references where applicable.
expectation.conceptual: Documentation authors should reference migrated Python issues through the supported GitHub issue-linking roles and treat the old Python bug tracker role as removed and unsupported.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to documentation build and authoring behavior. It should not alter pytest runtime APIs or test execution behavior, and supported GitHub cross-reference roles should remain available through the maintained documentation extension.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only change how documentation links are authored and resolved, without affecting normal library usage outside the docs toolchain.

behavior: The documentation configuration no longer loads the `sphinx.ext.extlinks` extension.
The `:bpo:` role is no longer available as a supported documentation role.
GitHub issue references are expected to use `:issue:` instead of the removed `:bpo:` role.
GitHub-oriented documentation roles are provided through `sphinx_issues`, including `:issue:` and `:pr:`.
acceptance_criteria: Given documentation authored for pytest 8.3.0, when a page uses `:issue:` for a GitHub issue reference, that role should be recognized as part of the supported documentation workflow.
Given documentation authored for pytest 8.3.0, when a page uses `:pr:` for a GitHub pull request reference, that role should remain part of the supported documentation workflow.
Given documentation authored for pytest 8.3.0, when a page uses `:bpo:`, that role should be considered unsupported and must not be relied on as an available cross-reference.

When legacy Python bug tracker references are migrated to supported GitHub issue references, the resulting change should affect documentation linking behavior only and should not change pytest runtime behavior.

task_32.title: Lint malformed `:user:` RST role usage in change notes
task_32.description: Version 8.3.0 adds contributor-facing pre-commit validation for change note content so typo-prone `:user:` RST role formatting mistakes are caught before documentation is merged or released. This improves release note authoring quality without changing library runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that contributor validation catches malformed `:user:` RST role usage in change note and release note bylines before documentation changes are accepted.

expectation.grounded: The upgrade should introduce pre-commit linting that checks change note content for incorrect `:user:` RST role usage, including formatting mistakes such as omitted backticks around the role target. Invalid `:user:` role syntax should be flagged during contributor validation, while this change should remain limited to documentation authoring workflows and not alter library runtime APIs or execution behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Authors should receive early feedback when user references in release notes are written with invalid `:user:` role syntax, preventing malformed documentation from being published while leaving normal library behavior unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce runtime-facing behavior changes, API changes, or execution differences in the library itself. Correctly formatted `:user:` role usage in change notes must continue to pass contributor validation without added side effects beyond the linting outcome.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve documentation authoring checks only, without changing how the library works for consumers or rejecting already valid release note content.

behavior: Pre-commit validation checks change note or release note authoring for typos in `:user:` RST role usage.
Malformed `:user:` role formatting in bylines is rejected during linting instead of silently passing through to published notes.
Correctly formatted `:user:` references remain accepted, and the library's runtime behavior is unchanged by this upgrade.
acceptance_criteria: When a contributor writes a change note with malformed `:user:` role syntax, the pre-commit validation should fail rather than allowing the note to pass unchecked.
When a contributor writes a change note with valid `:user:` role syntax, the pre-commit validation should allow the note to pass.
After upgrading from 8.2.2 to 8.3.0, library consumers should observe no runtime or API behavior changes attributable to this update.
